Read attributes, resolved along the hierarchy

Source: R/attributes.R
scale_attributes.Rd

With frame = NULL, returns the stored attribute table (filtered by attribute and source). With a frame, returns one row per member of that frame per attribute, resolved: a member's own value when it has one, otherwise the value of its nearest ancestor that has one, walking coarser frames one at a time. The row reports where the value came from in origin_frame/origin_unit; a member with no value anywhere gets an NA row.

scale_attributes(
  x,
  attribute = NULL,
  frame = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  inherit = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A NestedScale.

attribute

Character vector of attribute names; NULL for all.

frame

Frame whose members to resolve for; NULL returns the stored table unresolved.

source

Restrict to one source (or several). NULL uses whatever is stored and errors on a conflict.

inherit

Walk to coarser frames for members without a value of their own (default TRUE). FALSE reports stored values only.

Value

A data.frame with the attribute columns (frame, unit, attribute, kind, value, lower, upper, unit_of_measure, source, note), plus origin_frame and origin_unit when frame is given.

Details

Two situations are errors rather than guesses:

  • the walk reaches a frame where the member has several ancestors (the frames cross-cut) and at least one of them holds the attribute – "inheritance is ambiguous";

  • several sources publish the attribute for the same member and source is NULL – pass source= to choose.

Examples

s <- attach_attributes_scale(
  scale_example(),
  data.frame(frame = c("sector", "class"), unit = c("P", "S1"),
             attribute = "density", value = c(10, 5),
             unit_of_measure = "t/m3"),
  source = "survey", kind = "property"
)
scale_attributes(s)                           # stored rows
#>    frame unit attribute     kind value lower upper unit_of_measure source note
#> 1 sector    P   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 2  class   S1   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
scale_attributes(s, "density", frame = "unit") # resolved per atom
#>   frame unit attribute     kind value lower upper unit_of_measure source note
#> 1  unit   U1   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 2  unit   U2   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 3  unit   U3   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 4  unit   U4   density property    10    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 5  unit   U5   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 6  unit   U6   density property     5    NA    NA            t/m3 survey <NA>
#> 7  unit  OTH   density     <NA>    NA    NA    NA            <NA>   <NA> <NA>
#>   origin_frame origin_unit
#> 1       sector           P
#> 2       sector           P
#> 3       sector           P
#> 4       sector           P
#> 5        class          S1
#> 6        class          S1
#> 7         <NA>        <NA>
